title: Sprint 24 Planning

summary.overview: The team reviewed Sprint 23, which closed 31 of 36 points, and planned Sprint 24 around a 28-point capacity after accounting for Priya's leave. The headline commitments are shipping meeting search behind a feature flag, fixing the transcript scroll jank on long recordings, and moving the notification service off the legacy queue. Sofia flagged that the empty-state designs are still pending, so search will launch with a basic placeholder. The group agreed to keep a four-point buffer for production bugs and to hold a mid-sprint check-in on Wednesday of week two.

action_items.text: Create tickets for the search API and split them into estimable chunks
Deliver empty-state and no-results designs for meeting search
Profile the transcript list and ship the virtualization fix
Draft the migration plan for moving notifications off the legacy queue
Schedule the Wednesday mid-sprint check-in and share the board

transcript.summary: Looked back at what shipped, what slipped, and why velocity dipped.

transcript: Okay, let's get started. Thanks everyone for joining. The plan today is to look back quickly at Sprint 23, agree on capacity, and then pull in work for Sprint 24. We have about forty minutes, so I'll try to keep us moving.

Before we start, quick housekeeping. I updated the board last night so everything that rolled over is tagged, and I closed three tickets that were already done but never moved. So the carry-over list you see is accurate now.
Thanks Priya, that cleanup really helps. It's much easier to plan when the board reflects reality instead of what we remember from two weeks ago.

Sounds good. For the review, we closed thirty-one of thirty-six points. The five that slipped were all part of the export feature, and that was mostly because the CSV edge cases took longer than we expected.

Yeah, that was on me partly. We had transcripts with commas and line breaks inside the text, and the first version of the exporter just broke the columns. It's fixed and merged now, but it ate two days.

Honestly I'd call it a planning gap more than a mistake. We estimated it as a simple export, and nobody had actually looked at real transcripts with messy punctuation. Next time let's test with real data before we estimate.
Agreed, I'll grab a handful of the ugliest transcripts from the seed set and keep them as fixtures. That way any future export or import work gets tested against realistic text from day one.
No blame, that's a good catch to have found before a customer did. Liam, anything from the frontend side that we should call out from last sprint?

Two things. The new meeting card layout shipped and the feedback has been positive. But I noticed the transcript page gets really sluggish once a meeting is over an hour long. I haven't profiled it yet, I just feel it when I scroll.
I can confirm that. When I was reviewing the transcript view yesterday it stuttered on the long board meeting recording. It's not a design issue but I wanted to make sure it's on the radar.
It's definitely on the radar now. Let's treat it as a real item for this sprint rather than a nice-to-have. Priya, you mentioned notifications earlier this week?

Right. The notification service is still reading from the legacy queue, and that queue is going to be decommissioned at the end of next month. We don't need to finish it this sprint, but we should at least have a migration plan on paper.
Agreed. Let's put the plan itself into the sprint and the actual migration into the next one, depending on what we learn. Now let's talk capacity so we know how much room we really have.

transcript.summary: Worked out available points for the sprint after leave and agreed priority order.

transcript: I have Priya out Thursday and Friday of the second week, and Marcus has a half day for the dentist on Tuesday. Based on that I'm estimating twenty-eight points, which is a little under our average.
That sounds right to me. I'd also like to keep a four-point buffer for production issues. Last sprint we got pulled into two incidents and had nothing set aside, which is part of why export slipped.
Strong agree on the buffer. If we don't plan for interruptions we just pretend they won't happen, and then velocity looks worse than it is.

Could we also agree on what counts as an interruption? If a small bug takes twenty minutes I don't want to burn buffer on it, but if it eats an afternoon it should clearly come out of the four points.
Good distinction. Anything under an hour just gets done and isn't tracked. Anything longer gets a ticket and is logged against the buffer, so we can see at the retro where the time actually went.
Fine, four points of buffer, so twenty-four points of committed planned work. Let me share the backlog and we can go top to bottom. The first priority from the roadmap is meeting search.

Before we go deep on search, can I flag that the empty states and the no-results screen aren't designed yet? I have the main results list finished, but I've been pulled onto onboarding work this week.
That's useful to know. Can you get those to the team by Friday? Marcus and Liam can start on the happy path in the meantime and we'll slot in the placeholder states when they arrive.
Friday works. I'll keep them simple, just an illustration, a short message, and a suggestion to clear filters. Nothing fancy.
Perfect. Marcus, let's talk about how big the search backend work is, because I think that's the main unknown.

transcript.summary: Scoped the first version of search and agreed to ship it behind a feature flag.

transcript: So the plan is to use the full-text index we already set up on the transcript table. The query endpoint is probably eight points. That includes ranking, snippets with highlighted matches, and pagination so we don't return thousands of rows.
Eight feels reasonable but I'd split it. The snippet highlighting is the part I'd worry about, since it's easy to get subtly wrong with punctuation and different casing.
Fair point. I'll break it into a basic query endpoint, then snippets, then filters by date and speaker. That way we can demo something halfway through the sprint and cut the filters if we run short.
I like that. Can you create the tickets today so we can estimate them properly? I don't want to commit to eight points as one blob.
Yes, I'll do it right after this call and put estimates on each one so we can adjust before the sprint starts tomorrow.

On the frontend I'd estimate five points for the search page, the results list, and the input with debounce. If we put it behind a feature flag we can merge early and not worry about half-finished UI leaking out.
Yes, feature flag for sure. We ship it dark, test internally, and turn it on once Sofia's empty states are in. Anyone object to that approach?
No objection. One request though, please make the flag server-driven and not a hard-coded constant, so we can enable it for a subset of accounts without a redeploy.
That's easy enough, we already have the settings endpoint. I'll read the flag from there and default it to off.
From my side, should the flag also control the new search entry in the top navigation? I'd rather not show people a search box that leads nowhere while it's still in testing.
Yes, the whole entry point sits behind the flag, including the keyboard shortcut. Nothing visible changes for anyone until we turn it on, which keeps this safe to merge early.

transcript.summary: Decided to tackle transcript scrolling and plan the notification queue migration.

transcript: Next up is the transcript scroll performance. Liam, what's your gut on the cause and the size of the fix?

My guess is that we render every single segment as a DOM node, so a two-hour meeting has thousands of them. The standard fix is virtualizing the list so only the visible rows exist. I'd say three points, including making sure the auto-scroll with the player still works.
Just keep in mind the player sync. If rows are virtualized, you have to be careful that jumping to a timestamp scrolls to something that may not be rendered yet.
Good point, that's the tricky part. I'll write a small test with a long fixture so we can see the difference before and after.
Also worth checking memory use, not just frame rate. If we keep all the segment objects in state and only virtualize the rendering, a very long meeting might still be heavy on low-end laptops.
True, I'll test on the slowest machine I can find. My old laptop from last year should be a decent stand-in for what some of our customers use.
Great. Priya, the notification plan, how much do you want to take on this sprint?
Two points for the plan document. I want to list every consumer of the legacy queue, define the cutover steps, and work out how to roll back if something goes wrong. No code yet.

That fits. So that's search backend eight, search frontend five, scroll fix three, and the notification plan two, which is eighteen points. We have six points of room left in the committed twenty-four.

transcript.summary: Filled remaining capacity, named risks, and set a mid-sprint check-in.

transcript: I'd suggest we use the remaining six on the two small bugs from the support queue. The timezone display bug and the duplicate invite one both affect real customers.
Agreed. Those are two points each, which leaves two points unassigned. I'd rather leave that slack than overcommit, given that we already have the buffer.
I'm comfortable with that. My main risk is the search ranking taking longer than I expect, because I haven't tuned it against real data yet.
Okay, so let's name that as a risk. If ranking is not good enough by Wednesday of week two, we ship with basic relevance and iterate afterwards.
And my risk is the empty states, but that's covered since I committed to Friday. The only other thing is that I'll be reviewing the onboarding prototypes with Liam on Tuesday.
Noted. Last item, I'll set up a mid-sprint check-in for Wednesday of the second week so we can look at progress and decide if anything gets cut. I'll share the board link after the call.
Perfect, that gives us enough time to react if search ranking is slipping.
Alright, thanks everyone. Sprint 24 is set at twenty-four points with a four-point buffer. I'll send the summary and update the board within the hour.
